text:
With three seconds left in regulation, the Islanders' chance of beating St. Louis was about 1%. Victor Eklund changed that with a slap shot at 19:57 of the third, and New York went on to win 3-2 in a shootout. By our win-probability numbers, that single goal added half a win on its own, which is about as much as one shot can be worth.

It also felt fair. The Islanders had the better of almost everything: 76 shot attempts to 49, 3.77 expected goals to 2.10 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and a 77% share of the replays of every shot in the game. What kept St. Louis in it was Joel Hofer, the goalie who has taken the Blues' starting job from Jordan Binnington this month. Hofer saved about 1.8 goals more than his 29 shots deserved, including a 37% chance from Simon Holmstrom in the third. Jean-Gabriel Pageau's deflection had put New York ahead in the second; Dylan Holloway tied it from Robert Thomas, and Mason McTavish gave the Blues a 2-1 lead at 14:00 of the third that moved their win chance to 85%.

Then Eklund. The 2025 first-round pick, 16th overall out of Djurgardens, has been running hot (seven points in his last ten games against 4.7 expected), and his coach is leaning into it. "He's got ice in his veins," coach Peter DeBoer said of Eklund, per Stefen Rosner's post. Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat had the assists.

The shootout went the Islanders' way: Jake Neighbours scored for St. Louis, Mathew Barzal answered, Ilya Sorokin stopped McTavish, Horvat scored, and Sorokin turned away Holloway to end it. The Blues' four-game winning streak is over, but with Hofer playing like this, it is hard to read much into one shootout.
headline: Victor Eklund ties it with three seconds left
